subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should count as sufficient for this native-Linux constrained-VPS performance investigation?
rationale: The issue is actionable only after maintainers choose the measurement environment, runbook depth, and acceptance criteria across several core/runtime surfaces.

options.title: Runbook first
options.body: Publish a bounded measurement runbook using current telemetry and create narrow follow-ups only for measured missing spans or hot paths.

options.title: Narrow to one bottleneck
options.body: Retarget this item to one concrete bottleneck such as event-loop prep blocking or bundle-tools latency and leave the broader synthesis out of scope.

options.title: Close as support guidance
options.body: Treat constrained-VPS tuning as operational support and rely on existing VPS, memory, context, Telegram, and OTEL docs instead of adding a dedicated analysis.

recommendation.title: Runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded measurement runbook using current telemetry and create narrow follow-ups only for measured missing spans or hot paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent current-main history touches the most relevant runner timing and observability documentation surfaces.
